rationale:
Evidence: iteration 2 (kp 2.0, kd 0.8, base 1.3, 12 mm sensors at x -0.024..0.024) finished 20/20 on the oval (mean 1.91 s), but progress on the slalom stayed at 0.15 and the s-bend finished 1/20. Iteration 0 showed that kp 4 diverges. Slalom progress was about 0.13 to 0.15 at both kp 4 and kp 2, so gain level does not explain the slalom failure. The geometric diagnosis (the array spans only ±0.024 m, so the tape leaves the array at lateral offsets of about ±0.03 m and triggers line loss) is the hypothesis this round tests.

The round-1 critique is right on the arithmetic, and I accept it. The draft's kd/kp = 0.9/3.0 = 0.3, not 0.6. The ratio that actually ran stably was iteration 2's 0.8/2.0 = 0.4, so I use that ratio: kd 1.2 with kp 3.0. I also check the coverage claim. With 12 mm footprints at x = -0.04..0.04 (20 mm pitch), each sensor sees tape for offsets within about 0.0185 m of its position, so the union covers lateral offsets of about ±0.0585 m with no gaps. The draft's ±0.045 m figure was understated, and the 12 mm footprint already gives full coverage.

Kept: the wider array (x ±0.04, y 0.05), because it addresses the diagnosed line-loss cause directly. Weights -2..2, line_loss last_direction, ki 0, and body geometry are unchanged.

Changed or rejected: (1) sensor_size goes back to 0.012, not 0.016. The critique is right that a footprint change confounds the test. Coverage is already complete at 12 mm, so the footprint change is not needed to test the array width. (2) base_speed stays at 1.3, not 1.1. The critique's points hold: oval completion (500 points) is the largest term and was 20/20 at 1.3. A cut to 1.1 would probably cost completions on the s-bend and slalom, and it is a second variable on top of the geometry test. (3) kp rises to 3.0 with the wider 20 mm pitch to hold similar steering authority per unit of offset (about 2.0×83 ≈ 3.0×50). This is approximate, and I say so.

Expected result (guesses, not measured): the oval still finishes at about 1.9 to 2.1 s. Slalom progress should rise clearly above 0.15, and line_loss_events on the slalom should fall from 1.3 per run. Falsification rule: if slalom progress stays below 0.3 with line_loss_events still above 1, the tape-coverage hypothesis is wrong and the next round should look at the sensor lead (y) or the line-loss setting. If steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.3 (iteration 2 was 0.22), reduce kd toward 0.9. If the oval fails, return kp to 2.5.
